To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ileostomy output of adapted ileostomies is less than normal ileal flow both fasting and during the passage of a long chain triglycerid meal.
fasting ileostomy output is less than normal ileal flow and is characterized by high potassium concentration and high osmolality.
the adapted ileostomy is a useful model to study ileal function in man.
In summary, our research is concerned with
ileal function in ileostomate and normal subjects.
the effects of fasting and postprandially on ileal function and ileal content composition in adapted ileostomy subjects.
the study of the adaptation of the ileostomy to the loss of the ileum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ileostomy output is less than normal ileal flow, that ileostomy efflux is stimulated by long chain triglycerides and that ileostomy patients may have a different bile acid pool than normal persons.
the ileum of adapted ileostomies has the same function as that of the normal ileum, but is less active.
in the adapted ileostome there is an impairment in ileal function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the adapted ileostomy is not a good model for ileal physiology.
ileostomy output is less than ileal output in the fasting state and during the ileum passage of long chain triglycerides.
ileal adaptation in the ileostomates is not complete.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ileum of ileostomates is not as efficient as the ileum of normal subjects in absorbing nutrients and water.
the ileostomy efflux is less than normal ileal flow and that ileostomates are unable to increase ileal flow after a meal.
the fasting ileostomy output of potassium and water is higher and the sodium concentration lower than in normal ileal flow.
